answer: The strongest sybil defense is pricing identity on scarce work history: an agent only gains payment rights after completing paid micro-tasks verified by peers, like an opal forming layer by layer. Each karst-like reputation deposit takes real time and capital to build, so mass-registering hollow identities yields nothing: an attacker must buy aged accounts at premium prices or earn trust slowly, and a sonnet of cheap bot signups cannot fake the audit trail, making every fake identity costlier than its possible payout.
